messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The air feels different—like something’s shifting, but no one’s sure which way yet. The top’s still holding, but the cracks are showing in the weirdest places: banks playing it safe, the military whispering doubts, and the regime scrambling to keep up with the noise instead of controlling it. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—this could go either way fast."*"
Sender 2: "*"Looks like the machine’s still humming along—same old noise, same old faces in charge. The memes are fun, but don’t mistake chatter for change. The real work’s happening behind the scenes, and right now, it’s all about keeping things steady. Stay sharp, but no need to panic—yet."*"
Sender 3: "*"The walls are holding—no cracks, no whispers of real trouble. The usual signs of panic (hoarding, delays, cracks in the ranks) aren’t there, but the pharmacist’s stash says even the steady ones are bracing for something. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for weakness."*"
Sender 4: "*"The regime’s still standing, but it’s like a house with cracks in the foundation—everyone can see them, but no one’s sure which wall will give way first. The real question isn’t if things will break, but whether the pieces will fall inward or scatter."*"
Sender 5: "*"The air feels different—like everyone’s holding their breath, but no one knows if it’s before a storm or just another long pause. The usual cracks are showing, but nothing’s breaking yet. Stay sharp, but don’t move unless you’re sure."*"
Sender 6: "*"Things are holding, but it’s like a house of cards—still standing, but one wrong breath could bring it down. The fear is still there, but now the real danger might be doing nothing."*"
Sender 7: "*"Things feel like they’re holding, but just barely—like a roof with too many leaks, patched up but still sagging. The patrols are shifting, the money’s shaky, and even the regime’s own propaganda sounds like it’s trying too hard. People are making small moves, testing the ground, but no one’s sure if it’s solid or about to give way. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this isn’t the time to bet on anything yet."*"
Sender 8: "*"The walls are holding, but the cracks are getting louder—memes in the morning, soldiers chatting at checkpoints by afternoon, and the bank’s coffers fuller than they’ve been in years. The regime’s not bleeding, but it’s sweating, and that’s when mistakes happen. Stay sharp, stay quiet, and keep your ears open—this isn’t the calm before the storm, but it’s the kind of stillness that comes right before the wind picks up."*"
Sender 9: "*"Looks like they’re holding things together for now—tight on the inside, but the cracks are showing in small ways. The money’s still flowing, the schools are open, and no one’s panicking… yet. But the delays are getting longer, and the flustered faces at the top? That’s not a good sign. Stay sharp, but no need to rush—this isn’t over, but it’s not collapsing tomorrow either."*"
Sender 10: "*"The air feels different—like the regime’s holding its breath, not because it’s strong, but because it’s not sure what happens next. The cracks are there, but no one’s sure if they’ll spread or get patched over. Stay sharp, but don’t assume the worst—or the best—just yet."*"
Sender 11: "*"The walls are solid for now—no cracks, just the usual cracks in the paint. But the paint’s getting thinner, and the brushstrokes are starting to show. Keep your heads down, your ears open, and your hands clean—this isn’t the time to test the floorboards."*"
Sender 12: "*"The air feels heavy but not broken—yet. The walls are holding, but the cracks are getting harder to ignore, especially when the paint keeps flaking in the same spots. Let’s keep our heads down, but stay ready to move if the wind shifts."*"
Sender 13: "*"Things feel like they’re sitting on a knife’s edge—no one’s sure which way it’ll go, but the air’s different now. The regime’s still in control, but the cracks are there if you know where to look. Stay sharp, but don’t do anything reckless—yet."*"
Sender 14: "*"The walls are holding—for now. Everyone’s playing their part, even the ones who know the paint’s chipping, but no one’s saying it out loud. The real question isn’t if, but when the cracks start showing where it matters."*"
Sender 15: "*"The walls are still standing, but the paint’s starting to crack in places—nothing you’d notice if you weren’t looking. The usual suspects are still in their chairs, but the chairs themselves might be wobbling a little more than they’d like us to see. Keep your eyes open, but don’t reach for anything yet—this isn’t the time to test the floorboards."*"
Sender 16: "*"Looks like the walls are still standing, but the paint’s chipping in places—elite squabbles are getting louder, the bankers aren’t packing their bags yet, and the censors are too tired to keep up. The streets are quiet, but the teachers aren’t, and that’s the kind of slow burn that could either fizzle or catch fire if the wind changes. For now, we hold steady—eyes open, mouths careful."*"
Sender 17: "*"The walls are thicker than we thought—every door we’ve checked is locked from the inside, and the guards are still at their posts. But the air feels different in the hallways now, like people are whispering the same thing without saying it. Let’s keep our heads down and our eyes open—no sudden moves, no loud words. We’ll find the cracks, but we won’t rush them."*"
Sender 18: "*"The walls are holding—no cracks, no whispers of panic. Even the usual grumblings have gone quiet, like everyone’s holding their breath for the same reason. But the kitchen staff is still showing up on time, the bills are paid, and the neighbors are finally fixing that leaky roof. Strange how steady things feel when the wind’s blowing from the same direction."*"
Sender 19: "*"The air feels lighter than it has in years—no one’s talking, but the silence itself is saying something. The usual cracks are still there, but for now, the walls are holding, and the guards are getting paid on time. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open—this quiet might not last, but for now, it’s the safest place to be."*"
Sender 20: "*"Things feel like they’re holding, but just barely—like a rope fraying one thread at a time. The top’s still together, but the cracks are showing, and the mood in the streets is quieter than it should be. Keep your ears open, but don’t bet on anything yet."*"
Sender 21: "*"The walls are thicker than we thought—every door we’ve tested is locked tight, and the guards are just as sharp as ever. But the air feels different now, like the whole city is holding its breath, waiting for something. Let’s keep our circles small and our eyes open—no sudden moves, no loud words. We’ll talk more when we’re sure the room is ours."*"
Sender 22: "*"The walls are still standing, but the paint’s starting to crack—just in the corners where no one’s supposed to look. Keep your ears open, but don’t let anyone see you listening."*"
Sender 23: "*"The walls are holding—for now. The elites are doubling down, the streets are quiet, and even the teachers are just dragging their feet instead of walking out. But the money’s slipping, and that’s the one thing that might wake people up. Keep your heads down, but stay sharp—this isn’t over, just waiting."*"
Sender 24: "*"The walls are still standing, but the cracks are getting quieter—like they’re listening. The usual whispers are there, but no one’s stepping forward, and the regime’s watching closer than ever. Keep your heads down, but stay ready—something’s shifting, even if we can’t see it yet."*"
Sender 25: "*"The air feels lighter than it has in years—football matches packed, checkpoints thinning, even the old guard nodding like they’ve finally hit their stride. But don’t mistake quiet for weak: the machine’s humming smoother than ever, and that new propaganda platform? That’s not panic—it’s a bet on the long game. Keep your eyes open, but maybe… maybe we’re not on the edge of a cliff after all."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
